title: Customer Bridge Timeline and SLA Remediation Playbook
author: Arielle Gomez
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the customer bridge activation, timeline, and SLA remediation calculation for long-tail or high-impact incidents affecting Redwood Inference customers. It is intended for on-call operators, SREs, customer success managers (CSMs), and legal/exec comms. The goal is to ensure consistent, timely customer communication and a transparent remediation calculation when SLAs are impacted.

Audience and purpose:
- Audience: on-call SREs, bridge leads, CSMs, support engineers, account executives, legal.
- Purpose: standardize who does what and when during multi-hour or multi-tenant incidents; provide ready status and email templates; give a defensible, auditable SLA remediation calculation that can be shown to customers and finance.

Activation criteria (when to open a customer bridge):
1) Service severity triggers:
   - Severity A (outage) — >5 minutes of global unavailability for hosted API endpoints OR >2% customer impact as measured by error-rate spike above baseline.
   - Severity B (sustained degradation) — p99 latency breach for >30 minutes or error rate elevated >1% for >30 minutes.
2) SLA/contract triggers: any incident that pushes a customer’s monthly availability below their contracted SLA (e.g., 99.95% availability) for the current billing period.
3) Customer escalation: an enterprise customer requests a bridge or legal requests preservation of evidence.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Bridge Lead (assigned by on-call): coordinates timeline, messages, stakeholder invites, and decision authority for public updates.
- Technical Responder(s): own containment and remediation steps, provide estimates to bridge lead.
- Customer Liaison (CSM): owns customer-specific comms and post-incident reconciliation.
- Legal: verifies wording for regulated customers and signs off on remediation/comms when sensitive data or contractual terms are involved.
- Communications Owner (Go-to-market / PR): for incidents likely to require public blog posts or press coordination.

Bridge timeline template (use immediately on activation):
| Time after activation | Owner | Action | Output / Example |
|-----------------------|-------|--------|------------------|
| 0-5 min | On-call pager | Acknowledge pager, confirm activation | Conference bridge (Zoom/Meet) and Slack #bridge-channel |
| 5-15 min | Bridge Lead | Initial triage summary & impact estimate | Short status posted to status.redwood.ai and internal incident doc |
| 15-30 min | Technical Responder | Containment attempt (rollback/scale/bypass) | Failover or mitigation implemented (with commands) |
| 30-60 min | Bridge Lead + Customer Liaison | Customer-facing initial status | Initial template (see below) published + targeted email to impacted AEs/CSMs |
| 60-240 min | All | Regular updates every 30-60 minutes | Update cadence recorded; estimated ETA for recovery |
| Recovery | Technical Responder | Confirm recovery and validation | Monitoring checks green for 2x p99 window |
| +24-72 hours | CSM + Bridge Lead | Post-incident reconciliation and remediation calculation | Draft remediation proposal and schedule customer call |

Status cadence and content guidance:
- Tone: factual, concise, non-speculative. Avoid root-cause statements until validated. Use legal-safe phrasing: "We are investigating a service degradation affecting inference requests."
- Minimum contents of each public update: incident summary, scope/impact, mitigation in progress, next ETA, and a link to the status page.

Templates (copy-and-paste, replace placeholders):
1) Initial status page / email (30–60 min):
Subject: Redwood Inference — Service Degradation Affecting Inference API
Body:
We are investigating a service degradation affecting the Redwood Inference hosted Inference API (region: {region}). Some requests may receive elevated latency or errors. Our engineers are actively investigating and working on mitigation. We will provide an update by {ETA}.
Impact: {# customers affected or % traffic impacted}
Next update: {timestamp UTC}
Link: {status.redwood.ai/incident-id}

2) Follow-up update (every 30–60 min):
We have applied mitigations to reduce error rates. Request latency has improved in {regions}. We are continuing validation across traffic. Current impact: {reduced %}. Estimated time to full recovery: {ETA}.

3) Resolution message:
Subject: Redwood Inference — Service Restored
Body:
The service issue affecting the Inference API has been resolved as of {time UTC}. We validated recovery across {regions} and are monitoring closely. Impact summary and remediation calculation will be provided within 48–72 hours. If you experienced customer-facing impact, your CSM will reach out to coordinate next steps.

SLA remediation calculation (auditable):
- Principle: credits are computed per-customer, pro-rated for the portion of the billing period where actual availability < contractual SLA.
- Inputs required (collect at time of incident closure):
  - Customer contract SLA (A_sla) e.g., 99.95%
  - Billing period total minutes (M_period) e.g., 30 days = 43200 minutes
  - Customer observed downtime minutes (D_obs) = total minutes during billing period where service was unavailable for that tenant (use request logs and tenant ID filtering).
- Formula (credit percent of monthly fee):
  - Availability observed: A_obs = 1 - (D_obs / M_period)
  - If A_obs >= A_sla -> no credit.
  - If A_obs < A_sla -> Credit% = min(100, (A_sla - A_obs) / A_sla * 100)
- Example: 1-hour (60 min) tenant-affecting outage in a 30-day billing period with SLA 99.95%:
  - D_obs = 60
  - M_period = 43200
  - A_obs = 1 - (60/43200) = 0.998611 -> 99.8611%
  - A_sla - A_obs = 0.000539 or 0.0539 percentage points -> Credit% = (0.000539 / 0.9995) * 100 ≈ 0.05396% of monthly bill. Round to two decimals for customer-facing proposal.
- Rounding and minimums: finance requires credit proposals to be rounded to two decimal percent and minimum credit offered is $5 or 0.01% equivalent, whichever is higher.

Remediation decision matrix (high level):
- If incident is severity A affecting >5% of total traffic OR enterprise customer SLA breach -> automatic remediation review and phone call by CSM within 24 hours.
- If incident results in data loss or customer data exposure -> escalate to Legal + Exec and stop public language until approved.
- For minor transient spikes (<15 minutes, <0.5% impact) -> customer notification via status page only; remediation assessed in monthly review.

Post-incident workflow and deliverables (owner & timeline):
1) Within 24 hours: Bridge lead publishes incident chronology (who/what/when) — owner: Bridge Lead.
2) Within 48–72 hours: CSM drafts remediation proposal and credit calculation — owner: CSM + Finance review.
3) Within 5 business days: Post-incident review (internal) with SRE, Product, CSM; produce action items and assign owners.
4) Within 10 business days: Draft postmortem prepared and peer-reviewed; follow remediation schedule.

Evidence collection checklist (mandatory for remediation decisions):
- Request logs (tenant ID filtered) covering the incident window.
- Monitoring graphs: p95/p99 latency, error rates, host counts.
- Deployment and scaling events (timestamps & commands).
- Relevant runbook invocations and commands executed by responders.
- Communications archive (status page updates, emails to customers).

Runbook quick-steps (technical containment):
1) Identify top failing route(s) with request-id sampling.
2) Isolate knobs: reduce concurrency, enable fallback model variant, apply KV cache bypass/eviction plan.
3) If a deployment caused regression: rollback to last known healthy model version and monitor for 10 minutes.
4) If scaling is root cause: trigger emergency capacity (Dedicated burst or increase autoscaler target) and notify capacity@redwood.internal.

Customer comms escalation templates (CSM -> AE -> Customer):
- Short escalation email to AE: "Heads up: Incident {incident-id} impacting {customer-name}. CSM will follow up with details and remediation proposal within 48 hours."
- Phone script for enterprise call: open with apology, factual timeline, mitigation steps, remediation proposal, and expected follow-up. Keep duration <= 30 minutes for first call.

Game-day and rehearsal guidance:
- Frequency: quarterly cross-functional drills focusing on long-tail incidents and multi-tenant remediation calculations.
- Participants: on-call SRE, CSM, Finance rep, Legal, and an Exec sponsor.
- Metrics to practice: evidence collection time (target < 4 hours), remediation proposal time (target < 48 hours), and customer ack time (target < 24 hours).

Templates for the status page (short form):
- Title: "Investigating: Inference API Degradation"
- Summary: "We are investigating elevated error rates for inference requests. Impacted customers may see increased latency or errors."
- Updates: timestamped bullets with concrete mitigations.

Decision logs and auditability:
- All bridge decisions must be recorded as timestamped entries in the incident doc, including who approved remediation and the inputs used for the SLA credit calculation. Attach finance-ticket number when credit is applied.

Review cadence and ownership:
- This playbook is owned by Customer Success. Review annually or after any incident where remediation was >0.5% of monthly bill.
- Suggested reviewers: SRE (operations), Product (model-serving), Finance (billing), Legal (contracts).

Appendix A — Template remediation worksheet (CSV columns):
- customer_id, contract_sla_percent, billing_period_minutes, observed_downtime_minutes, observed_availability_percent, credit_percent, proposed_credit_usd, finance_ticket_id

Appendix B — Example chronology excerpt (internal):
- 2026-05-12T09:03Z — Pager fired: elevated 500 errors on inference-prod-us-east-1.
- 2026-05-12T09:06Z — Bridge opened (Zoom/Slack #bridge-123).
- 2026-05-12T09:22Z — Mitigation: rollback model v1.3.2 -> v1.3.1; error rate dropped 70% within 8 minutes.
- 2026-05-12T11:00Z — Recovery validated.

End of playbook. For questions or to request an enterprise-specific variant of this playbook, contact the Customer Success playbook owner: arielle.gomez@redwood.internal.
